business_scope.primary_industry_name: Product Interface Design and Digital Design Subscription Agency

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 1258/2008 (SAS regime); Decree 410/1971 (Código de Comercio); Law 526/1999 (UIAF creation); Law 1121/2007 (CFT measures); Decree 1674/2016 (beneficial owner definition); DIAN Resolution 000091/2021 (mandatory UBO register); Law 1437/2011 (administrative procedure appeal rules).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney or incorporation mandate executed by each UBO/shareholder in favor of the local incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction; Colombian notary if executed in Colombia
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for foreign-origin documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Authenticated copy of certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant foreign companies registry or corporate register in the shareholder's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and notarized UBO/PEP declaration for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority; notary public of the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization when notarized abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence of foreign UBO or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and legal representatives against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Colombian UIAF money-laundering/terrorism-financing risk lists. Mandatory enhanced due diligence for all politically exposed persons (PEPs), regardless of jurisdiction of residence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification. Ongoing sanctions re-screening required at onboarding, at each material transaction, and at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) via Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be registered in Spanish or in a Latin-alphabet transliteration; non-Latin scripts are not admitted. The name must contain or end with the designator 'S.A.S.' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. Foreign words are phonetically transliterated into Spanish spelling where required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition with the same Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days of notification under Articles 73–80 of Law 1437/2011, attaching a revised proposed name and supporting justification. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the competent administrative court. A parallel fresh name reservation may be filed using a materially different name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for SAS registration and for the design-as-a-service industry, provided the company maintains a real physical Colombian address for service of process and official notifications. The virtual office must be operated by a registered provider able to receive notices from DIAN, Cámara de Comercio, and judicial authorities. No industry-specific physical workplace is statutorily required for UI/UX design subscription services.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk; estimated annual probability of unannounced physical inspection is below 10% for a low-risk design subscription entity. The likelihood increases to approximately 15–20% if the company triggers transfer-pricing review, invoicing anomalies, late UBO filing, or repeated AML/CFT reporting discrepancies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Ley de Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas), Arts. 1-5, 17 and 45; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), Arts. 110 and 354; Decreto 1074 de 2015 (regulatory commercial decrees); Ley 1429 de 2010 (formalization incentives); Estatuto Tributario, Art. 555-2 (RUT obligation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) acting through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUE) and Registro Mercantil; supervised by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document), executed by all founding shareholders, authenticated before a notary or accepted through the Chamber's virtual registration channel, and inscribed in the Registro Mercantil pursuant to Art. 4 of Ley 1258 de 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Colombian S.A.S. The incorporators freely fix the subscribed capital in the bylaws; share capital must be fully paid within one year of subscription (Art. 5, Ley 1258 de 2008). No escrow account is mandated at the national level; deferred cash contributions and in-kind contributions must be expressly described with valuation in the incorporation document.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION - [Company Name] S.A.S. RESOLVED: 1. Share Subscription: The issuance and subscription of the company's authorized share capital, as stated in the incorporation document, is ratified. 2. Registered Office: The registered office is fixed at [Address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia; all statutory and judicial notices shall be served at this address. 3. Officers: [Name] is appointed Legal Representative and Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] is appointed Treasurer, with full authority to execute client agreements, open bank accounts, and direct payment operations. 4. Compliance: The Legal Representative is authorized to obtain the NIT and RUT from DIAN, register the company as employer, and complete all filings required by the Cámara de Comercio. This resolution takes immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Homonymy Certificate (Certificado de Homonimia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) via the online RUE portal at www.ccb.org.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Chamber's online consultation system and submit up to three proposed corporate names for the SAS. The system verifies the absence of identical or confusingly similar registered entities. After confirmation, download the official Certificado de Homonimia, which remains valid for 30 calendar days and must be presented during registration.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (up to 3 alternatives)
Copy of national ID or passport of each founding shareholder
Company profile: business activity (ISIC 7410), domicile, intended capital
Contact email address for the RUE portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is occupied or flagged as confusingly similar, immediately submit alternative names; the homonymy certificate can be reissued for the new name without payment of additional research rights.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Private Incorporation Document (Documento Privado de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or the Chamber of Commerce standardized formation module; Notary Public if public deed form is elected
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the bylaws and incorporation document containing all mandatory particulars of Ley 1258 de 2008: corporate name, domicile, duration, business purpose, subscribed and paid capital, share classes, governance rules, corporate books, and dissolution provisions. Have all founding shareholders sign the instrument and authenticate their signatures before a notary or through the Chamber's virtual notarization channel.
required_dossiers: Valid homonymy certificate issued by the Cámara de Comercio
Draft incorporation document and bylaws
ID documents of all subscribing shareholders
Statement of capital subscription and payment schedule
Optional: appraisal report for in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber or notary observes defective or non-compliant clauses, prepare a corrective private document (documento aclaratorio) signed by all shareholders and re-submit for authentication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registration with the Chamber of Commerce (Registro Mercantil / RUE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del Domicilio Social - Registro Único Empresarial (RUE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed incorporation document together with the homonymy certificate and pre-RUT data at the Chamber's service window or through the RUE online portal. Pay the registration rights and mercantile registry tariff. Upon approval, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal and assigns the provisional NIT for the company.
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation document with authenticated signatures
Homonymy certificate
Shareholder ID copies
Pre-RUT data sheet
Proof of payment of registration rights and fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration receives observations (observaciones) or rejection, remedy the cited defects within the Chamber's cure period (generally 10 business days), adjust the document, and re-submit with any applicable fee difference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and NIT Registration with DIAN (RUT, Electronic Signature, E-invoicing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - online portal www.dian.gov.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the DIAN virtual portal using the provisional NIT issued by the Chamber. Complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT), selecting tax responsibilities: corporate income tax, national withholdings, VAT if applicable, and municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA) through the local mayor's office. Activate the electronic invoicing system (facturación electrónica) and obtain the digital signature of the Legal Representative.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Provisional NIT assigned by the Chamber
Legal representative's identification
Company activity codes: CIIU 7410
Registered office address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT application is rejected or flagged, file a correction (aclaración) through the DIAN portal, rectify the CIIU code or tax-responsibility fields, and confirm the electronic signature activation before re-submitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the Corporate Bank Account and Disbursement of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank (e.g., Bancolombia, Davivienda, BBVA Colombia) under Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the selected bank with corporate and KYC documentation. Open a commercial checking account in the company's name and enroll the digital subscription payment rails (Stripe Billing, Wise) for recurring client billing. Deposit the paid-in portion of the share capital, if any, and preserve the deposit receipt in the corporate minutes as evidence of capital payment.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
NIT / RUT
Certified copy of bylaws
Legal representative's ID and KYC / UBO forms
Proof of registered office address (public utility bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects or queries the application under KYC rules, complete the beneficial-owner form, adjust the capital deposit proof, or apply to another licensed credit institution with updated corporate documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration, Social Security Affiliation and Occupational Safety Clearance (SG-SST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL), EPS, Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones (AFP), and the Ministerio del Trabajo via the PILA system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer through the PILA integrated payroll platform (Planilla Integrada de Liquidación de Aportes), affiliating the Legal Representative and any staff with the selected ARL, EPS, and AFP. Adopt the basic Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) in accordance with Decreto 1072 de 2015, and obtain the fire-safety clearance for the office premises from the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos.
required_dossiers: NIT / RUT
Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Legal representative's ID
Registered workplace address
Employee payroll data (if staff are hired)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the PILA employer registration fails due to a NIT mismatch, rectify the RUT with DIAN first and re-submit the planilla; contact the ARL to adjust any affiliation date and avoid retroactive liability.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 7410 (specialized design activities) is a non-industrial, office-based professional service. No industrial or manufacturing license is required from MinCIT or its attached regulatory entities; general authorization derives from the Registro Mercantil and the municipal commercial zoning certificate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing license required for a design subscription agency. The right to operate is evidenced by the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation, the municipal Certificado de Uso de Suelo (land-use certificate), and compliance with the design-industry professional and data-processing standards applicable to the UI/UX subscription model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) and Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (municipal environmental authority) - reference only
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based design studio classified as low-impact services (Category III); no environmental impact assessment, environmental license, or environmental registration is triggered under Decreto 1076 de 2015 and Ley 99 de 1993 for ISIC 7410 activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOCs, or stationary combustion emissions are generated. Office solid waste must be segregated and managed under the municipal PGIRS waste-management rules; electronic waste (e-waste) from design hardware must be surrendered to licensed recycling operators as required by municipal environmental decrees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must obtain the fire-safety certificate of the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos under Ley 1575 de 2012; satisfy the structural load, electrical, and egress conditions of the building; implement the workplace safety plan (SG-SST) under Decreto 1072 de 2015; and maintain emergency exits, portable extinguishers, smoke detection, and first-aid provisions proportionate to the office headcount.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN). Official self-service portal: Muisca (muisca.dian.gov.co); general portal: www.dian.gov.co; e-invoicing endpoint: factura.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned S.A.S.: (1) Incorporate by private document and file for registry with the Cámara de Comercio of the city of operations, including the online pre-RUT submitted with the incorporation; (2) Upon Chamber registration, DIAN auto-assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and issues the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) consolidating income tax, VAT, and customs status; (3) Appoint the local legal representative, tax accountant and, if legally triggered, the revisor fiscal; (4) Obtain the qualified electronic signature (certificado de firma digital) from an authorized CA (e.g., Certicámara, GSE, Vita) and activate the DIAN e-invoicing program; (5) Complete the UBO/beneficial-owner filing and open a local bank account with foreign-exchange code for export proceeds. Foreign shareholders must evidence passport, foreign tax ID, and address, and file the FATCA/CRS tax-domicile self-certification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the S.A.S. is a limited-liability corporation taxed at entity level on Colombian-source and worldwide income (Impuesto sobre la Renta, 35% for FY 2024) and subject to the 19% IVA regime; pass-through treatment is unavailable to corporations, although the optional SIMPLE regime may consolidate income and payroll taxes for eligible small entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: U.S.-style check-the-box election does not exist under Colombian law. Statutory elections available: (i) SIMPLE regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación, Law 2010/2019 and Law 2277/2022) for entities with annual gross income ≤ 95,000 UVT; (ii) hybrid-mismatch alignment election under Article 585-1 E.T. (Law 2277/2022) allowing the domestic taxpayer to adjust deductions or inclusions where a hybrid entity or instrument creates a deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction result with a foreign jurisdiction; (iii) election for a foreign non-resident to operate through a Colombian permanent establishment instead of capitalizing a local S.A.S.; and (iv) mutual agreement procedure (MAP) elections in transfer-pricing disputes. No check-the-box recognition of foreign U.S. partnership or S-corporation classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas) — single national value-added tax governed by Decree 1625/2016 (Decreto Único Reglamentario), Article 420 et seq. of the Estatuto Tributario, and Law 2277/2022; no separate state or municipal sales tax exists in Colombia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for services: under Article 930 E.T., every business providing taxable services in Colombia — including ISIC 7410 UI/UX design subscription services — must register as an IVA responsible party (RUT/NIT) before the first transaction, regardless of turnover. The petty-trader simplification (annual sales ≤ 600 UVT) applies only to individual sellers of goods, not to corporate service providers. The SIMPLE regime (elected up to 95,000 UVT annual gross income) does not waive full VAT registration; it only consolidates the income-tax and payroll-tax side.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing through DIAN-approved invoicing software or the free Muisca facturador; each invoice is transmitted in real time over DIAN web services (SOAP/REST), validated, and returned with the CUFE code and status 'validada' (tax-clearance equivalent). The invoice must contain a certified digital signature, QR/URL verification, and mandatory data fields under Resolution 165/2023. Electronic credit and debit notes and the RADIAN (Registro de Activos Digitales) clearing log complete the fiscal-control cycle; API integration and a DIAN-approved contingency procedure are mandatory for subscription-based recurring billing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating under Article 481 E.T. for services requires: (1) the contractual recipient is a non-Colombian company or entity with no permanent establishment in Colombia; (2) the service is executed in Colombia but used and economically exploited exclusively abroad (for design-as-a-service this is demonstrated by deliverables sent to the foreign UI/UX client, a global SaaS subscription model, and foreign-market licensing/usage); (3) the fee is actually collected in convertible foreign currency through the Colombian foreign-exchange market; and (4) the service is not excluded by Article 481's specific list or subject to the local digital-services VAT block. Law 2277/2022 tightens the cross-border digital-services test: the service must not ultimately be used by a Colombian-based user of the foreign client. The exporter must maintain a service-export file (expediente) with the contract, legalized invoice, exchange declaration, and the client's tax-domicile certificate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX, electronic Form 92 DIAN) for physical goods; for services, the Colombian 'Declaración de Exportación de Servicios' registered in the RUT/DIAN export profile
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing physical dispatch where goods accompany the service
Export services contract in Spanish/English identifying the non-resident beneficiary and the exclusive foreign-use clause
Commercial export invoice (CUFE electronic invoice with zero-rate line and IVA exclusion code)
Declaración de Cambio (FX settlement form) submitted through the Colombian authorized foreign-exchange intermediary
Inward remittance certificate / SWIFT credit advice or bank statement evidencing collection from the foreign client within 180 days
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN runs systematic triangulation of RUT status, CUFE invoices/RADIAN records, DEX declarations, and FX settlements. Improper zero-rating exposes the exporter to: (i) VAT assessed at 19% of the fee plus moratory interest retroactive to the billing date; (ii) 'sanción por inexactitud' of up to 200% of the greater tax due (Article 647 E.T., as amended by Law 2277/2022); (iii) criminal fiscal fraud penalties, including imprisonment of 36 to 72 months and fines of 150%-200% of the tax evaded; (iv) joint and several liability of the legal representative and revisor fiscal; and (v) foreign-exchange administrative fines for non-repatriation or non-channeling of the export proceeds beyond the 180-day deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia ('Banco de la República' / 'BRC') is the central bank and foreign-exchange authority, with the Junta Directiva issuing monetary and exchange regulations; the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia ('SFC') supervises licensed foreign-exchange intermediaries and enforces AML/CFT (SARLAFT); DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) controls tax registration, beneficial-owner reporting, and trade/exchange declaration integrity. Core legal instruments: Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1068 of 2015, BRC Resolution 8 of 2000, and BRC Regulatory Circular DCIN-83.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is freely convertible at market rates referencing the TRM (representative market rate) published by the BRC. Current-account operations, including export of UI/UX design services, are liberalized but subject to mandatory channeling through authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries ('intermediarios del mercado cambiario' / IMCs) and filing of standardized exchange declarations. Capital-account flows, including foreign equity investment into a Colombian S.A.S., require no prior BRC authorization for the design-services sector but must be channeled through an IMC and registered with the BRC on Form No. 5 (Declaración de cambio por inversiones internacionales). Unregistered foreign investment cannot legally remit dividends or repatriate capital. Profit remittances are permitted once the investment is registered (Registro de Inversiones Internacionales) and after payment of the applicable dividend withholding (currently 10% on dividends paid out of already-taxed profits and 35% on dividends paid out of untaxed profits under E.T. Art. 245, as amended by Law 2277 of 2022) and company income taxes; no separate remittance tax applies. Convertibility is therefore high, but operational compliance is time-sensitive and document-intensive.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia no longer mandates forced conversion into COP; the applicable duty is repatriation and channeling. Proceeds from exported services (including DaaS subscriptions) must be collected within six (6) months from the date of service performance (Art. 12, Decree 1735 of 1993, as codified in Circular DCIN-83). Collections must be (i) channeled through an IMC and declared on Form No. 1, (ii) deposited into a BRC-authorized foreign-currency compensation account ('cuenta de compensación') held abroad, or (iii) held in a foreign-currency account at a Colombian IMC. There is no statutory surrender/ conversion ratio; 100% of proceeds may be retained in USD if held in a compliant compensation or IMC foreign-currency account. Each collection requires the IMC to file Form No. 1 with the supporting commercial invoice and service contract. Late or non-channeled export proceeds constitute a foreign-exchange infraction sanctionable by the SFC.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational COP account plus USD account at the IMC (cuenta de compensación) and foreign-investment registration desk
Operational COP account plus USD current account for export collections and Form No. 5 investment channeling
Operational COP account plus USD account with integrated FX forward capability and digital treasury APIs
Operational COP account plus limited USD compensation-account service
Operational COP account linked to Scotiabank's North American USD network

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as an ancillary collection-and-conversion rail; Low as a standalone treasury solution. Colombian law recognizes only locally licensed 'Sociedades Especializadas en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos' (SEDPEs) under Law 1735 of 2014; foreign EMIs (e.g., FCA-regulated payment institutions) cannot passport banking status into Colombia. Wise's Colombian operating entity, Wise Colombia S.A.S., is an SFC-supervised SEDPE and is not a bank; balances carry no deposit insurance. The S.A.S. may use Wise to receive USD payouts from Stripe Billing, convert into COP, and sweep funds into a Tier-1 IMC account, provided every flow is reconciled to the Form No. 1/Form No. 5 channeling obligation within the six-month export-collection window. Holding export proceeds indefinitely in Wise balances without BRC authorization for a compensation account violates channeling rules. Shareholder capital injections must never be routed through Wise or Stripe; they require direct SWIFT to the IMC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is normally mandatory for the local legal representative of a newly incorporated S.A.S. to sign the SARLAFT customer-due-diligence file and the account-opening minutes at an IMC branch. Bancolombia and BBVA offer partial remote/video onboarding for existing digital clients, but for an entity newly organized with non-resident shareholders, the bank compliance committee typically requires at least one physical interview with the resident legal representative. Non-resident shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) can avoid travel by granting an authenticated power of attorney (notarial, apostilled under the Hague Convention) to the resident representative; the attorney's physical attendance then suffices. Banks further require biometric or physical identity verification of authorized signatories and, for higher-risk structures, verification of UBO identity. Practical recommendation: appoint a Colombian domiciled legal representative with banking mandate authority so all onboarding appearances can be completed locally within 5-10 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly created S.A.S. with zero operating history, foreign-only shareholders, and immediate expected high-volume international subscription revenue from Stripe/Wise rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation issued by the local Chamber of Commerce (within 3 months); RUT (Registro Único Tributario) issued by DIAN; notarized bylaws with capital allotment; 12-month projected P&L and expected treasury flows; signed subscription or service agreement with the first anchor clients; DIAN ultimate beneficial-owner registration (Beneficiario Final resolution); board resolution appointing treasury signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Funnel risk: payment aggregation through Stripe Billing and Wise generating many low-value inbound credits inconsistent with a declared low-risk DaaS business model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe merchant agreement and billing-product configuration; daily settlement reconciliation file; breakdown of client geographies and invoice volumes; underlying customer contracts and deliverables (Figma/Jira/Asana project evidence); written treasury policy committing to 5-business-day sweeping into the IMC account; names of principal beneficiaries of the aggregated flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: non-resident shareholders residing in jurisdictions without public company registers or use of layered intermediate holding vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed SARLAFT customer-onboarding form and certified identity/address of every natural-person UBO; notarized ownership-structure diagram of the ultimate parent; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration for the equity injection; DIAN Beneficiario Final filing confirmation; passport copies and recent utility bills of UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP flags: nominee directors, shared registered addresses, or name matches with politically exposed persons or adverse media.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dated negative-news screening report and OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening result; signed non-PEP declarations by all shareholders, directors, and signatories; where a PEP is identified, a SARLAFT enhanced-due-diligence file with source-of-wealth evidence and compliance-committee approval memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payment risk: remittances to a broad set of foreign freelancers and cloud/tooling vendors that could be mischaracterized as currency arbitrage, profit stripping, or financing of the parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master vendor register with corporate identifiers and local VAT/GST registrations; recurring service contracts with unit economics and payment calendars; project-management records linking invoices to accepted deliverables; commitment to provide each vendor invoice and Form No. 1 back-up documentation within five (5) business days of any wire; transfer-pricing policy documentation for any related-party service payments to keep the thin-capitalization and arm's-length rules satisfied.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity or shareholder-loan inflows must enter through a Tier-1 IMC account in the S.A.S.'s name. Routing: foreign parent → SWIFT MT103 to the IMC beneficiary account, wire reference stating purpose code 'Inversión directa de capital – suscripción de acciones' or 'préstamo de accionistas'; the IMC may convert USD to COP at the day's TRM or hold proceeds in a USD account at the IMC. The investment must be declared on Form No. 5 (Declaración de cambio por inversiones internacionales) through the IMC, which registers the investment with the BRC within five (5) business days of the transaction and issues the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales (RII) confirmation. Simplified registration applies if the investor's cumulative foreign investment is below USD 500,000 equivalent; above that threshold, the IMC requires notarized shareholder resolutions, investor identity documents, and full UBO disclosure. The S.A.S. treasury file must retain the stamped Form No. 5, the incoming MT103, the shareholder subscription minutes, and the RII certificate because the certificate is the legal precondition for all future dividend remittances and capital repatriation. Shareholder loans must respect the 3:1 debt-equity thin-capitalization limit under E.T. Art. 118-1 and must be registered with term and interest-rate schedule. Capital injections must never be delivered through Wise, Stripe, or other non-IMC channels.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 in USD or COP via the IMC for (i) service-import payments to offshore contractors and software-tooling vendors, supported by Form No. 1 (Declaración de cambio por operaciones de cambio) with commercial invoice and contract; and (ii) dividend and profit remittances to the non-resident shareholder, declared on Form No. 5 with the RII reference and DIAN-documented dividend availability. Secondary rail: Wise (SEDPE) business payouts for micro-disbursements below USD 50,000 to payees lacking SWIFT access, funded only from proceeds already compliantly channeled into the IMC system. Commercial letters of credit are not a practical instrument for DaaS subscription disbursements and should be reserved for exceptional procurement of licensed software or hardware from non-investment-grade suppliers, executed as a 90-day sight or deferred LC; the underlying FX payment still requires the corresponding Form No. 1 declaration. Every outbound payment requires that the applicable Colombian withholding tax (e.g., 15% for services rendered by non-residents under E.T. Art. 408) and any service-export e-invoicing obligations have been cleared, so treasury must synchronize with the DIAN accounting calendar. Hedging and derivatives must be executed exclusively with IMCs, be linked to genuine underlying trade exposures, and be documented in a board-approved treasury policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD deliverable outright forwards with an IMC, notional tied to forecast USD subscription collections and net cash-flow gaps.
COP/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in COP against the TRM, permissible onshore through IMCs when dollar settlement is not desired.
COP/USD cross-currency swaps used to hedge principal and interest flows on shareholder loans or software-asset financing.
Vanilla purchased FX options (COP/USD call or put) to cap adverse rate movements without losing upside; option writing is generally restricted for non-financial operating companies.
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) to bridge timing differences between USD subscription collections and COP operating disbursements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social principal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through March 31 of each calendar year; no extension for S.A.S. entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a penalty calculated on the Chamber's registration tariff plus monthly interest on arrears; failure to renew for two consecutive calendar years authorizes the Cámara de Comercio to cancel the commercial registration, resulting in administrative strike-off and loss of the entity's presumed operational continuity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Shareholders' Approval (Estados Financieros y Aprobación de la Asamblea de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio, as annex to the registry renewal documentation after approval by the shareholders' meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year closes on December 31; financial statements must be presented, approved, and contained in the registry renewal submission no later than March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of timely shareholder approval invalidates the financial statements for statutory and filing purposes and creates administrative liability for the company's directors; submission of renewal without the required accounting documentation will be rejected and may expose the entity to the same two-year registry cancellation procedure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory for an S.A.S. when: (a) total gross assets or gross ordinary income at the end of the prior fiscal year exceed 5,000 SMMLV (current minimum legal monthly wages); (b) the company has 30 or more shareholders; or (c) the entity is a parent, subordinated, or public-interest-type company subject to permanent supervision by the Superintendency of Companies. A low-risk UI/UX design subscription S.A.S. below these thresholds is not subject to a compulsory independent audit, though financial statements must be certified by a public accountant and the legal representative whenever external reporting or mandatory audit conditions apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NIIF (IFRS) as adopted by Colombian law through Law 1314/2009 and DUR 2420/2015; the applicable standard is full IFRS for Grupo 1 large entities or NIIF for PYMES (IFRS for SMEs) for a typical design-subscription service S.A.S., unless classified as a micro-entity under Grupo 3 and legally allowed to use simplified local accounting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once annually, and in conjunction with the commercial registry renewal, the S.A.S. must confirm the accuracy of its shareholding structure and disclose final beneficial owners (natural persons with direct or indirect control or 5% or greater ownership) in the corresponding final-beneficiary declaration to DIAN. Any share transfers made during the year must be reflected in the Register of Members before the annual confirmation is filed; the absence of a transfer does not excuse the annual confirmation obligation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors and Legal Representatives (Libro de Registro de Directivos y Representantes), if applicable
Shareholders' Meeting Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea General de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – USD 600 per year for a registered office address and corporate agent in Bogotá or Medellín.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 7,000 for a certified independent audit of a small-to-mid-size design-subscription S.A.S. when the audit is compulsory.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 35% corporate income tax rate for Colombian S.A.S. entities. A 7-year income-tax exemption may be available for qualifying creative and cultural activities under the Orange Economy framework (Law 1955/2019), subject to compliance with employment, investment, and revenue thresholds. Entities may also claim an additional deduction of up to 25% of qualifying investments in science, technology, and innovation activities. The S.A.S. is not subject to the additional 3% financial-sector surtax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) filed electronically through the DIAN Muisca portal using the entity's NIT and registered electronic signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; taxpayers may be required to make advance prepayment installments of income tax during the year based on the prior year's net tax liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year is generally the calendar year. The annual return is due in the following calendar year according to the DIAN published schedule, determined primarily by the last digit of the NIT; deadlines typically fall between early April and early May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT, taxpayer identification number, and principal address of the Colombian S.A.S.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. must use the Colombian NIT issued by DIAN; the foreign parent or non-resident tax ID is not used as the primary taxpayer identifier unless the entity is a foreign legal person with a Colombian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from all business operations, including recurring UI/UX design-as-a-service subscription fees, license fees, and ancillary service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue recognized for Colombian accounting and tax purposes must be reported, including amounts invoiced to non-resident clients through Stripe or Wise payment rails.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Devoluciones, rebajas y descuentos: returns, refunds, rebates, and discounts granted on subscriptions and service contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident client adjustments must be supported by contracts, credit notes, and bank settlement records; failing to evidence the deduction may trigger inexactness penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos de venta: direct costs attributable to producing design services, including designer salaries, freelance subcontractor costs, software tools, hosting, and production assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cost reimbursement deductions are allowable only if the S.A.S. has full supporting documentation and if cross-border payments to related parties comply with transfer-pricing standards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gastos de administración y ventas: general administrative and marketing expenses, including office rent, administrative payroll, subscriptions, accounting and legal fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-resident shareholders, subordinated loans, or foreign service providers will be scrutinized for economic substance, arm's-length pricing, and proper withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta exenta: exempt income such as qualifying Orange Economy creative-industry income for the statutory exemption period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim this exemption on a look-through basis; the benefit is recognized only at the Colombian S.A.S. level if statutory requirements are timely documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto a cargo: final national income tax liability, applying the 35% statutory rate to taxable income after losses carryforward and allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resulting tax is the amount credited against dividend distributions and is the basis for determining any foreign tax credit available in the shareholder's jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing imposes a sanction of 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due. If no tax is due, the late-filing sanction is computed on gross income or net equity using UVT-indexed rates. Incorrect returns may trigger an inexactness penalty of 160% of the omitted or evaded tax. Late payment carries interest and may lead to asset seizure by DIAN.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders where the distribution is sourced from profits already subject to Colombian corporate income tax; if the distribution is sourced from untaxed or preferentially taxed profits, the additional withholding may rise to 35%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief is not automatic. The Colombian payor must obtain a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the non-resident shareholder's domestic tax authority, duly legalized or apostilled where required. The foreign shareholder must confirm beneficial ownership, provide a declaration of absence of Colombian permanent establishment, and submit any additional forms required by DIAN. The payor must keep the TRC and supporting documentation for audit purposes and file the reduced-rate withholding report through the Muisca portal.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on interest paid to non-resident financial creditors is generally 15%, and statutory WHT on royalties paid abroad is generally 33%. Under an applicable DTA, interest may be reduced to 5-15% and royalties to 5-10% depending on the treaty partner and beneficial-ownership conditions. Payments for software or design-related IP subscriptions may be characterized as royalties if the transaction transfers usage of copyrighted work; the S.A.S. should obtain technical legal analysis before invoicing cross-border IP fees.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer-pricing documentation applies to taxpayers carrying out transactions with foreign related parties when the aggregate value of those transactions exceeds COP 450,000,000 in the taxable year. Additional TP information returns and Local File/Master File obligations may apply based on the entity's gross income, net equity, or multinational group revenue thresholds as indexed by the DIAN UVT system.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not maintain a formal Economic Substance Regulations registry comparable to UAE-style regimes, but DIAN applies substance-over-form, general anti-avoidance rules, and anti-abuse doctrine. An S.A.S. with no real staff, physical presence, business decision-making, or genuine economic activity may be disregarded for tax purposes, cross-border payments may be recharacterized, and DTA relief may be denied for lack of beneficial ownership or economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating UI/UX subscription revenue, fabricating expenses, using fake invoices, destroying accounting records, or otherwise evading the 35% corporate income tax by submitting a materially inaccurate Form 210.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion is sanctioned under Colombian Criminal Code Articles 426-427 with imprisonment of up to nine years and fines; administrative penalties include 160% of the omitted tax plus late interest and indexing. DIAN may also suspend registration and initiate criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, and statutory auditors who knowingly sign false returns may be jointly and personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax. Personal assets may be attached, travel bans may be issued, and implementing officers may face imprisonment. Civil restitution may extend to the full amount of tax harm caused.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing foreign related parties for UI/UX design subscriptions at non-arm's-length prices, creating artificial margins, or failing to file the mandatory transfer-pricing documentation for cross-border related-party transactions above the COP 450,000,000 threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may re-price the transaction on an arm's-length basis, disallow deductible expenses, and impose an inexactness penalty of up to 160% of the additional tax. Failure to submit TP documentation triggers separate daily/UVT-based fines and potential criminal referral for tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign intercompany agreements with inflated or deflated prices may be held personally liable for the resulting tax adjustment, face director disqualification, and be exposed to criminal tax evasion charges if the conduct is proven intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Entity and Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Colombian S.A.S. as a mere invoice pass-through or conduit with no real employees, no business premises, no operational decision-making, or no substantive delivery of design services, particularly when claiming treaty benefits or transferring profits abroad as royalties/dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the entity for tax purposes, disallow expenses paid abroad, recharacterize distributions as taxable income, impose penalties for abusiveness, and deny DTA benefits. The entity may also be reported to the Financial Information and Analysis Unit for potential money-laundering or shell-company typologies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may lose the corporate-veil limitation if the S.A.S. is used as a sham; personal liability may include civil restitution of avoided taxes, travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment for tax fraud or criminal conspiracy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Stripe or Wise payment rails to receive subscription fees while bypassing Colombian foreign-exchange and tax-reporting requirements, failing to disclose beneficial owners, or moving proceeds to foreign accounts for laundering, illicit enrichment, or financing of prohibited activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money-laundering offenses under Colombian Criminal Code Article 323 carry imprisonment of 10 to 30 years and fines. Administrative AML fines and sanctions may be imposed by UIAF; failure to report foreign exchange operations may generate additional tax and customs penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and legal representatives who knowingly facilitate or fail to prevent laundering through subscription transactions face criminal liability, disqualification from commercial activity, travel bans, asset seizure, and personal restitution orders. Beneficial owners cannot shield assets through the S.A.S. corporate form.
